summary: Alien is a Grasshopper (Rhino 8) plugin: a node whose logic lives in a plain Python 3 or C# script file, with pins and on-node controls from a header comment. Describe a node in plain English and a model writes the script, runs it and fixes its own errors. Nodes are shareable files; AI agents drive everything through a built-in MCP server. It ships with a suite of architectural nodes and keeps what they generate in a library.

node.summary: One Alien node runs one script file. Saving the file (or a model or agent editing it) rebuilds the pins, keeping wires by name, and re-solves.

example: # NODE_INPUTS: base:Curve, count:int | "divisions" min=2 max=200 default=20
# Divides a curve into N points.
rules: First 200 lines; Python uses #, C# uses //. Several NODE_INPUTS / NODE_OUTPUTS lines are allowed.
Token: name:type [| "description"] [min= max= step= decimals= default= options="a|b|c" suggest="p"] [button] [image]. Commas inside quotes are fine.
Access: list[T], T[], T:list -> list; tree[T] -> tree (a list of branch lists); otherwise item.
Pin names are identities: renaming one drops its wires.
Outputs are generic; a type after : documents them.
After the pins: an optional # CATEGORY: line (a library category label), then one comment line saying what the node does (its library listing).
Python packages: # r: numpy (first 32 lines). C# references: // r "full/path.dll" or // r "nuget: Name, 1.2.3".
header.types: float int bool str Color Interval Point3d Vector3d Plane Line Circle Arc Box Rectangle3d Curve Surface Brep Mesh SubD Geometry Transform object (aliases: double/number, string/text, point, vector, domain, colour)

values: An unwired input gets, in order: its manual value (from the node's control or MCP set_values), the header default, else None / [] (C#: default(T)).
An input set to its header default holds no manual value.
Outputs are top-level variables with the output names; nested lists become data trees; tuples, sets, generators and numpy arrays become lists; Polylines become PolylineCurves.
Item-access inputs fed with lists run the script once per item.

Takes an image file or link dropped on the node (its path or URL) and shows a thumbnail; typing a path or URL works too.
A list drawn under the text box follows the typing (Vicmap addresses, about 0.1 s a lookup, from the street number on); arrow keys + Enter or a click pick one.

how: The request, the current script, earlier requests for the node and summaries of the wired inputs go to the model, which returns the whole file.
Alien writes it (the old version goes to .alien/history), re-solves and judges the run report: an error, unset outputs, no outputs or every output empty goes back to the model. Up to 4 attempts.
Progress shows on the node and in the panel; every request is kept in the node's transcript.

From a selection: each selected node's id, header (or component name), output summaries and one building record in full go with the request; the model answers with a 'WIRES: input <- id.output; ...' line and Alien wires the new node before its first judged run. MCP generate takes the same as context: [ids].

The MCP server listens on loopback only and refuses non-loopback Origins; any local process can still call it, including run_code. Don't expose the port.

Terrain: Geoscience Australia 5 m LiDAR DEM where it covers the site, gaps filled from the statewide Vicmap Elevation 10 m DEM; surface models (Terrarium, Open-Meteo) only if both fail. A 2 m grid, at most 201 x 201 points.

Streets: each centreline gets a cross-section from its road class, fitted to the road reserve measured from Vicmap road casement polygons (property line to property line). Carriageway, median, nature strip, footpath; lanes (reserve <= 7.5 m) wall to wall with no kerb; verges paved in central/commercial zones (CCZ, CDZ, ACZ, C1Z, MUZ, DZ, PDZ). Bands and reserves are overlaid into planar regions, classified, meshed and draped on the ground; verges sit a 150 mm kerb above the road, with kerb faces between.

Trees: Vicmap Vegetation Tree Urban points with LiDAR height and canopy half-widths, modelled by shape: broad (clumps of lumpy low-poly blobs on a split trunk with limbs), columnar, eucalypt (open high crown), conifer (stacked cones) or palm (trunk and fronds), from the species where known (City of Melbourne) else from proportions, seeded per tree. Trees under 1.5 m get a height from their canopy; points inside a building footprint reading roof height are left out.

Geometry is in metres scaled to the model's units, centred on the site, Y = true north. z = 0 is the ground at the site centre (datum gives its AHD height). Curves stay flat at z = 0 for modelling; ground, buildings, streets and trees follow the terrain.
Fetched data is cached for 30 days in the temp folder (alien-cache/vic_site_map), each v2 layer on its own; refresh (a button) fetches again once.
Data is fetched for a context bucket (60, 120, 200 or 300 m) and trimmed to the radius, so sliding the radius within a bucket refetches nothing.
The address field suggests Victorian addresses while typing (Vicmap address index, about 0.1 s per lookup).
If Vicmap's ArcGIS property/parcel layers fail (as after a republish on 12 Oct 2026), the same layers are read from the open-data WFS and info says so.

mcp.server_instructions:
Alien: Grasshopper nodes backed by script files (Python 3 or C#) in the user's script repository.
Pins come from header comments ('//' instead of '#' in C#):
  # NODE_INPUTS: pts:list[Point3d], n:int | "count" min=1 max=50 default=5
  # NODE_OUTPUTS: curves, log
Unwired input -> manual value (set_values) -> header default -> None/[] (C#: default(T)). Outputs are top-level variables with those names; nested lists become data trees.
Loop: canvas -> add (python|csharp|any GH component; nodes+links for a whole chain) -> wire -> script_edit (returns ok/error+line/output summary) -> inspect / capture.
Pick Python for quick iteration and libraries; C# for heavy loops (simulations, 100k+ items) or strict typing.
Rhino side: doc (context, save, import), objects (list/select/zoom), layers (tree, visibility, materials), view (camera, display), rhino (commands, find, help). search finds GH components.
Ids are the 8-char ids from canvas/objects (a unique nickname also works for nodes). docs(topic) has syntax, types, gotchas.

tools.name: canvas
tools.description: Compact graph of the active Grasshopper document: nodes (id, type, name, state, pins; sel = selected by the user), wires 'src.out>dst.in' and named groups.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: 'alien', 'errors', or a name substring. Default: everything.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Include pins of native components too.

parameters.name: solve
parameters.description: Recompute the whole definition first and report errors/warnings.

tools.name: add
tools.description: Place a node. component='python'|'csharp' creates an Alien node with a new script in the repository (or attaches `script`); any other value places that Grasshopper component by name or search id (e.g. 'Number Slider', 'Panel'; 'Category:Name' when plugins share a name). Returns id, pins and (Alien) the first run report. Whole chains: `nodes` (each {key, component, name?, script?, code?, x?, y?, values?}) plus `links` ('key.out>key.in', keys or ids) in one call.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: 'python', 'csharp', a Grasshopper component name, or an id from search

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Initial script source (Alien). Omit for a starter template.

parameters.name: script
parameters.description: Attach an existing script instead (repo-relative or absolute path).

parameters.name: near
parameters.description: Place to the right of this node id

parameters.name: links
parameters.description: Batch: wires between the new nodes (keys) and existing ids

tools.name: wire
tools.description: Connect (or disconnect) wires. Each link is 'srcId.outputParam>dstId.inputParam'; the param part may be omitted for single-pin nodes and sliders/panels. Links that would create a loop are refused.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Drop each target input's existing wires first (links in this call still accumulate)

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Remove nodes from the canvas (script files are kept).

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the Grasshopper component library: every word must appear in a name, nickname, description or category. Returns 'Name [nick] (Category/Sub) id'; pass the id to add when names clash. detail=true (or a single hit) lists the top hit's inputs and outputs.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words to match, e.g. 'curtain wall cell'

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Restrict to a tab/category, e.g. 'VisualARQ' or 'Curve/Division'

tools.name: script_read
tools.description: Read an Alien node's script. With from/to, returns numbered lines only.

tools.name: script_edit
tools.description: Change an Alien node's script and wait for Grasshopper to re-solve. Either `edits` (exact find/replace, each `old` must match once) or full `code`. Previous version goes to .alien/history. Returns the run report.

tools.name: generate
tools.description: Describe-a-node: a model (OpenRouter, or 'ollama:<name>' locally) writes the script from plain English, runs it and fixes its own errors. Omit id for a new node; on an existing id the request edits its script. Returns attempts, cost and the run report.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Alien node to change (omit to create one)

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Nodes the new node works with: the model sees what they output and wires them in

parameters.name: near
parameters.description: Place to the right of this node id

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Summarise a node's data: Alien run report + input sources, or any component's outputs (counts, types, ranges, bbox, samples).

tools.name: set_values
tools.description: Set values and re-solve. Alien: manual values for unwired inputs by name (null clears). Slider: {value,min,max,decimals}. Panel: {text}. Toggle: {value}. Value List: {value: item name}. Any other component: values for its unwired inputs by nickname (arrays = several items). `preview` shows/hides viewport preview of any node(s).

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description: Show (true) or hide (false) the node's viewport preview

tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Run a throwaway Python 3 or C# snippet inside Rhino (API exploration, document queries). Returns printed output and the value of `result` if assigned.

tools.name: capture
tools.description: PNG of the Rhino viewport (default) or the Grasshopper canvas. Camera/display options are the same as `view` but apply to this capture only; the user's view is restored unless keep=true.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: true/'extents', 'selected', or a box [[x,y,z],[x,y,z]] (extents is the default when `view` is given without camera/focus)

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Leave the viewport at the new camera/display afterwards

tools.name: view
tools.description: Set the active Rhino viewport without capturing (persistent): view preset, camera/look_at, lens, projection, display mode, zoom or focus. Returns the resulting camera.

tools.name: objects
tools.description: Rhino document objects. Filter by ids (8-char or full), layer (includes sublayers), type, name (substring), selected, hidden. action 'list' (default: counts by type/layer, bbox, first `limit` rows 'id type layer name'), 'select' (replaces the selection) or 'zoom' (frames them in the active view).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: point, pointcloud, curve, surface, brep, extrusion, mesh, subd, block, annotation, hatch, light

tools.name: layers
tools.description: Rhino layers. Without `path`: the layer tree with object counts, flags and materials. With `path`: creates the layer if missing, then applies visible, locked, current, color, material (a document material name, a Rhino material-library search like 'Glass brick' or 'Matte Steel', or {color, transparency, gloss}).

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: List only layers whose path contains this

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Layer colour '#RRGGBB' or a colour name

parameters.name: material
parameters.description: Material name / library search string, or {color, transparency 0-1, gloss 0-1, name?}

tools.name: doc
tools.description: Rhino + Grasshopper documents. action 'info' (default: file, units, counts, selection, active view, GH document, versions), 'save' (both documents in place), 'save_copy' (`path`: .3dm copy or export by extension, `gh_path`: .gh copy; documents keep their own paths), 'import' (merge a file into the Rhino document), 'open_gh' (open `path`, or the editor with a blank document), 'plugins' (third-party Rhino plug-ins and Grasshopper libraries).

tools.name: rhino
tools.description: Run a Rhino command and return what it printed; without arguments, return recent command-line history. find: command names containing text. help: the command's help page from docs.mcneel.com.

parameters.name: find
parameters.description: List command names containing this, e.g. 'va' or 'array'

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: Command name to look up, e.g. 'ArrayCrv'

tools.name: bake
tools.description: Bake a node's output data into the Rhino document (anything bakeable: geometry, plugin objects). Objects are tagged; by default the node's previous bake is deleted first, so re-baking replaces instead of duplicating.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: Output name (default: all outputs; for sliders/params: the node itself)

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Target layer full path, e.g. 'Model::Walls' (created if missing; default current layer)

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Delete this node/param's previous bake first (default true)

tools.name: docs
tools.description: Alien reference. Call with no topic for the topic list.

tools.name: repo
tools.description: Script repository: show root and scripts, or set the root folder. library=true: nodes by category with descriptions, plus generated assets.
